about.title: Personal Injury Help in Citrus Heights, California
about.longDescription: Citrus Heights sits in the northeast corner of Sacramento County, a city of about 87,000 people whose daily traffic funnels along Greenback Lane, Sunrise Boulevard, Auburn Boulevard and Antelope Road. In 2025, public records list 310 injury collisions inside the city limits. Those crashes left 408 people hurt, and three people died. The reports also show a pattern: collisions tend to bunch up on Wednesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters are heading home. Behind each of those counts is a person trying to sort out medical bills, a damaged car, and an insurance adjuster who calls before the bruises have faded. That is where we come in. Our team handles personal injury claims directly. We do not charge you a fee unless there is a recovery. If you were injured in a crash, a fall, or another incident someone else caused, you can reach out today and talk it through with our team, who can explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Citrus Heights Claim

items.title: The clock runs for two years
items.desc: California gives most injury victims two years from the date of harm to file a lawsuit. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, that window can shrink to six months for the required government claim.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut you out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Even if you were partly to blame, you can still recover; your share of the fault simply reduces the amount.

items.title: No ceiling on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, lost enjoyment of life, and emotional distress. What those losses are worth depends on your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes in Citrus Heights tend to happen?
items.answer: According to public collision records, the corridors with the highest counts are Greenback Lane, Antelope Road, Auburn Boulevard, and Sunrise Boulevard. Reports also cluster on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are simply record counts reflecting where and when traffic is heaviest, not a judgment about any particular street.

items.question: How long do I have to bring an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of the injury. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or a public sidewalk, you may have only six months to file a formal claim first. Our team can confirm which deadline applies to you.

items.question: What if the police report says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible does not end your claim. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it is not eliminated. We can review the report and the evidence rather than taking the initial assessment at face value.
